name: shame
description: Deep dismay about how an action has (or will) resulted in unwanted negative judgment from others about an important social rule. It lowers your sense of self-worth and predicts a long-term loss of social status.
perceptions: I broke an important social rule, bringing major negative attention to myself.
I did not want this type of attention.
I may lose status in a social relationship from this.
examples: I forgot my best friend's birthday and she's irritated about it.

guidance.description: Many people experience a pattern of shame that is enduring and pervasive. Learning to meet shame with self-compassion is key to altering this pattern.
guidance.attribution: Michaela B Swee and Susan Murray

variations.name: shaming someone
variations.description: Taking action to point out someone's behavior as breaking an important social rule.
perceptions: That person is not following an important social rule.
They don't seem to recognize the gravity of this.
Someone needs to enforce that rule.
results: Taking an action to remind someone about the rule.

guidance.description: Using shame to get others to do what we want is easy, but damaging.

variations.name: unwarranted shame
variations.description: A sense that someone is trying to reduce your social status for something minor or something you didn't do.
perceptions: Someone is claiming that I broke an important rule.
I did not, or don't agree the supposed infraction was important.

guidance.description: Unjustified public shaming shouldn't make you question your self-worth.

commentaries.quote: Shame is the most powerful, master emotion. It's the fear that we're not good enough.
Whatever is begun in anger, ends in shame.

Heightened self-consciousness, apartness, an inability to join in, physical shame and self-loathing—they are not all bad. Those devils have been my angels. Without them I would never have disappeared into language, literature, the mind, laughter and all the mad intensities that made and unmade me.
Patriotism demands the ability to feel shame as much as to feel pride.
